title: How to improve Excel efficiency for data analysts: a guide for Mac users

description: Learn how to optimize your Excel workflows on Mac. Discover why inefficiency happens, the real costs of manual work, and practical fixes for data analysts.

intro: Data analysts use Excel as their primary workspace for quick data validation, cleaning, and ad-hoc reporting. While it remains a staple in the industry, many analysts struggle with manual processes that drain time and introduce errors into critical business reports.
tldr: 76% of data analysts still rely on spreadsheets for data preparation.
Manual data entry and cleaning tasks account for 80% of an analyst's time.
Up to 94% of complex spreadsheets contain errors that lead to bad business decisions.
You can optimize your workflow by using Power Query and keyboard shortcuts.
Lazur helps you stay in flow by answering questions about Excel features out loud.

blocks.text: Why Excel efficiency matters for your career

You likely spend hours every week copy-pasting data, fixing formatting issues, and chasing down broken formulas. This is not just a nuisance. It is a fundamental barrier to your actual work. When you spend 80% of your time cleaning data, you have very little time left to provide the insights your team needs. Excel is a powerful tool, but it is often used in ways that do not scale. If you are doing the same manual cleanup every Monday morning, you are losing time that could be used for modeling or strategy.
The hidden costs of manual spreadsheet work

The costs are not just about your time. There is a financial cost to the business. When models contain errors, they lead to incorrect decisions. These decisions can cost companies millions. A small error in a formula or a broken link can ripple through an entire report. If you are working with sensitive information, always check your company policy on data handling. Never upload protected data to public AI tools. Keep your analysis safe by following your internal security guidelines.

The problem often starts with how we are taught to use the tool. We learn to use Excel for small tasks and then try to use those same methods for enterprise-scale data. Excel is not a database. When you push it beyond its limits, it slows down and becomes unstable. You might notice that your workbook crashes when you add a few thousand rows. This happens because the file structure is not designed for heavy data processing. It is also common to rely on manual copy-pasting instead of using built-in features like Power Query. When you do things by hand, you are prone to fatigue. Fatigue leads to mistakes.

items: Use the Data tab to access Power Query. It automates your data cleaning steps.
Learn keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + ⌥ + V for paste special.
Use Flash Fill to standardize data entries without writing complex formulas.
Keep your raw data on a separate sheet from your analysis.
Use named ranges to make your formulas easier to read and debug.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Excel files for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps. It points at things on your screen and explains how to do them yourself.

faq.question: Is it safe to use Lazur with company data?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Content is never used to train AI models. Always follow your employer's rules regarding sensitive data.
